overall_summary: The channel's clear breakout niche is extreme space phenomena, specifically exotic exoplanets with bizarre weather or physical properties (e.g., raining rubies, burning ice, coal-dark atmospheres). These videos consistently generate the highest view counts (700 to 1,000+ views) and engagement rates. Conversely, standard psychology and brain facts are severely underperforming, rarely crossing 100 views unless framed with a mind-bending physics twist (e.g., time dilation aging the head faster than feet). Visual, sensory-rich, and high-stakes cosmic concepts are driving the channel's current momentum.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Exoplanet Weather & Sensory Space Anomalies
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' achieved 1,016 views and 36 likes. 'The Planet of Burning Ice' reached 1,055 views. 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' generated 721 views and 25 likes.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on exoplanets with extreme, hostile environments, focusing on sensory descriptions (smell, sight, touch, weather) and high-contrast visuals.

winning_patterns.pattern: Mind-Bending Physics Framed as Personal Biology
winning_patterns.evidence: 'Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet' (relativity/time dilation) achieved 263 views, vastly outperforming standard brain facts.
winning_patterns.action: When covering physics or space-time concepts, frame them using the human body or daily life as the reference point to increase immediate relatability.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' struggled with multiple uploads getting between 5 and 53 views. 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' stalled at 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from textbook psychology facts. If covering the brain, it must connect to a shocking external mystery or cutting-edge technology (like the Pink Floyd brain wave recreation).

weak_patterns.evidence: 'This Star Is Older Than the Universe!' got only 11 views, and 'The Star Colder Than Ice' got 82 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid purely mathematical or abstract astronomical facts that lack strong, immediate visual hooks or tangible environmental hazards.

next_video.concept: WASP-12b, the pitch-black egg-shaped planet that is actively being stretched and devoured by its parent star.
next_video.opening_direction: Start with a high-contrast visual of a distorted, egg-shaped planet glowing with molten heat: 'Right now, there is a pitch-black planet in our galaxy shaped like a giant egg because its own star is literally eating it alive.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet is so dark it absorbs 94% of light, making it look like a cosmic void, and it only has a fraction of its life left before it is completely swallowed.
next_video.reason: Aligns perfectly with the top-performing exoplanet trend (TrES-2b and burning ice). The 21-second format matches the duration of the channel's most successful recent uploads, allowing enough time to build a compelling narrative arc without losing retention.

experiment: Test a 'What If' scenario focusing on cinematic animal survival in extreme environments (e.g., 'What If You Were Trapped in a Pit with 1,000 Hibernating Wood Frogs?'), bridging the gap between the high-performing animal facts and high-stakes survival storytelling.
